tineBlockRef.language: Language used by this extension's messages, hovers, panels and tool results. Note: command titles and setting names follow the VS Code display language and cannot be overridden here.
tineBlockRef.language.enum.auto: Follow the VS Code display language (default)
tineBlockRef.graphRoot: Tine graph root directory. Leave empty to auto-detect a directory that contains both pages/ and logseq/.
tineBlockRef.include: File patterns to index, relative to the graph root.
tineBlockRef.exclude: Paths to exclude from indexing. Tine / Logseq metadata and recycle bins are excluded by default.
tineBlockRef.maxDepth: Default depth for expanding nested block references (a reference inside another referenced block). 0 disables recursion.
tineBlockRef.maxOutputChars: Output character budget for a single tool call. Content beyond it is truncated with a notice.
tineBlockRef.hoverPreviewLines: Number of block content lines shown in the hover preview. Fewer lines keep the popup short, so the Expand and Backlinks buttons at the bottom stay visible.
tineBlockRef.hideProperties: Property names to hide when rendering block content (without the trailing ::).
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.enabled: Show ((uuid)) inline as the target block's first line, similar to native Tine / Logseq rendering. When disabled, the raw UUID is shown.
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.mode: Inline rendering mode. If the cursor misbehaves in replace mode, switch to append.
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.maxTitleLength: Maximum length of the target block title in inline rendering. Longer titles are truncated with an ellipsis so the line does not grow unbounded.
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.showMissing: Show "⚠ Block not found" inline instead of the raw UUID when the target block is missing, so broken references stand out immediately.
tineBlockRef.render.stripHeadingMarks: Strip Markdown heading marks (#, ##, ...) from block titles in inline rendering, hover preview and expanded documents. Content returned by AI tools keeps the marks so the model can still read the hierarchy.
tineBlockRef.showIndexNotification: Show a notification in the status bar area once the index has been built automatically. When disabled, a warning is still shown if the index is empty (no notes found).
tineBlockRef.backlinks.style: How backlink counts appear in the editor. Only blocks that are actually referenced show a marker, so most notes gain nothing.
tineBlockRef.backlinks.panel: How the backlinks panel is rendered. Links inside a text editor require Ctrl+Click (a VS Code rule); only the webview panel supports plain left-click.
tineBlockRef.backlinks.subtreeLines: Maximum subtree lines expanded per referencing block in the backlinks panel. 0 means unlimited (default), matching Tine. A few blocks in real vaults exceed 400 lines; set a value such as 30 to truncate them.
tineBlockRef.backlinks.itemsPerPage: Maximum references listed per page in the backlinks panel. The remainder is summarised so a heavily referenced block does not produce an endless panel.
tineBlockRef.backlinks.pathDepth: Number of ancestor levels shown as the breadcrumb for each referencing block. Deeper ancestors are dropped, keeping those closest to the reference.
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.mode.enum.repl: Hide the raw UUID and show only the target block title (closest to native note-app rendering)
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.mode.enum.appe: Keep the raw UUID and append 〔target block title〕 after it (more conservative, cursor behaves normally)
tineBlockRef.backlinks.style.enum.inline: Show a "🔗 N" badge at the end of the block line; hover it to list pages that reference the block. Matches Tine (default)
tineBlockRef.backlinks.style.enum.lens: Show "N link references" on a separate line above the block. Use this when VS Code inlay hints are disabled (editor.inlayHints.enabled)
tineBlockRef.backlinks.style.enum.off: Show no backlink marker in the editor; the commands still work
tineBlockRef.backlinks.panel.enum.html: Webview panel: left-click a block title to jump, styled after Tine (default)
tineBlockRef.backlinks.panel.enum.text: Read-only text document: requires Ctrl+Click to jump, but supports Ctrl+F and free copying

tineBlockRef_readBlock.modelDescription:
Read the real content that a block reference (a UUID such as ((uuid))) points to in a Tine / Logseq note.

When you see ((66c73a56-ddda-44d2-80dd-009e44406fd4)) or {{embed ((66c73a56-...))}} in a .md note, you must call this tool to learn what it points to — the UUID itself carries no semantic information.

Returns: the target block's first line, all child blocks with their hierarchy preserved, the source file and line number, and the subtree size. If the target block does not exist the result says so explicitly (dangling reference). If the same UUID is defined in several places, all candidates are listed.

Use when: understanding what a "see ((uuid))" in a note means, expanding a block's entries, or tracing knowledge across files.
Not for: reading an entire note (use blockNote) or resolving [[page name]] links (not handled by this tool).
tineBlockRef_readBlock.blockIds.descript: UUIDs of the blocks to read, at most 20. A (( )) wrapper is accepted and stripped automatically.
tineBlockRef_readBlock.includeChildren.d: Whether to include child blocks. Defaults to true. Child blocks usually carry the actual content, so keep this enabled unless you only need the first line.
tineBlockRef_readBlock.compact.descripti: Compact mode: output only the first line of each block, useful for scanning many blocks quickly. Defaults to false.
tineBlockRef_readBlock.maxDepth.descript: Depth for expanding nested block references (a reference inside another referenced block). Defaults to the extension setting (3). 0 disables recursion.
tineBlockRef_readNote.modelDescription:
Read an entire Tine / Logseq note and expand every ((uuid)) block reference in it into its real content.

**When you need to read a .md note under pages/ or journals/, prefer this tool over the plain file-reading tool**: a plain read only shows a string of UUIDs, hides the referenced content, and will make you miss key context and draw one-sided conclusions.

mode parameter (important, directly affects output size):
- expand (default): expand the whole note. When there are more than 8 references a list is attached automatically; content beyond the output budget is not expanded and the unexpanded line numbers are listed at the end.
- list: **return only the reference list** (line number, UUID, target block first line), usually just a few KB. When there are many references (>10), or you only need to locate one, **prefer this mode** and then read specific blocks with blockRef.
- both: list plus expanded content.

Usage advice:
1. When unsure how many references a note has, start with mode=list.
2. Use mode=expand when you need the actual content.
3. If the result says some references were not expanded, read those UUIDs one by one with blockRef rather than falling back to plain file reading.

Content is generated in memory; no file is created or modified. If the file is open in the editor with unsaved changes, the current editor content is used.
tineBlockRef_readNote.filePath.descripti: Path to the note. Either an absolute path or a path relative to the graph root, for example pages/some-note.md.
tineBlockRef_readNote.includeChildren.de: Whether to include child blocks when expanding. Defaults to true.
tineBlockRef_readNote.maxDepth.descripti: Depth for expanding nested references. Defaults to the extension setting (3).
tineBlockRef_findBacklinks.modelDescript:
Find which notes reference the given block UUID (backlinks).

Use this to answer questions such as "where is this block referenced", "who cites this content", or "does this content appear elsewhere".

Returns, for each referencing location: file, line number, reference type (inline / embed), and the first line of the containing block. The definition location of the UUID is also given; duplicate definitions or a deleted target block are called out explicitly.
tineBlockRef_findBacklinks.blockId.descr: UUID of the target block. A (( )) wrapper is accepted.
tineBlockRef_findBacklinks.limit.descrip: Maximum number of references to return. Defaults to 50, maximum 200.
